label: Standard Sequence
desc: The universal trunk: Fundamentals → Common Practice → Chromaticism → Post-Tonal. All students follow this spine.

tiers.label: Tier 1 — Fundamentals & pitch reading
tiers.desc: Staff literacy, rhythm, intervals, basic voice leading. Pre-tonal.

units.title: Scales & key signatures
units.feat: Major, minor forms, circle of fifths

units.title: Cadences
units.feat: AC, HC, DC, PC — harmonic goals

units.title: Non-harmonic tones
units.feat: PT, NT, SUS, APP, ET, ANT, PED

tiers.label: Tier 2 — Common practice harmony
tiers.desc: Core diatonic → early chromatic. Backbone of the two-year Theory I–II sequence.

units.title: Chords with the Third in the Bass
Chords with the Fifth in the Bass

tiers.label: Tier 3 — Late romanticism & extended chromaticism
tiers.desc: Chromatic saturation, enharmonic reinterpretation, tonal ambiguity.

tiers.label: Tier 4 — Post-tonal theory
tiers.desc: Early 20th century through serialism, spectralism, and beyond.

units.title: Pitch-class sets I
units.feat: PC sets, normal/prime form, Forte labels

units.title: Twelve-tone serialism I
units.feat: Row forms: P, I, R, RI; matrix

units.title: Diatonic modes
units.feat: Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, etc.; modal harmony

tiers.label: Tier 5 — Jazz & contemporary tonal
tiers.desc: Jazz harmony, improvisation theory, pop/film, and analysis of vernacular styles.

units.title: Jazz chord symbols & voicings
units.feat: Lead sheet symbols, drop-2, shell voicings

units.title: Reharmonization
units.feat: Tritone subs, passing chords, Coltrane changes

units.title: Modal jazz
units.feat: So what voicings, quartal harmony, suspended dom

units.title: Post-bop & free jazz
units.feat: Upper structures, outside playing, free rhythm

label: Branch A — Figured Bass (Handel model)
desc: Optional parallel track preceding Roman numerals. Progressive introduction of figures following Handel's exercises (Ledbetter ed., nos. 1–24). Teaches the same harmony as Tier 2 but from the thoroughbass side.
prereq: Tier 1 complete. Bridge unit A15 connects back to Tier 2 Roman numeral notation.

tiers.label: FB-1 — Foundations
tiers.desc: 5/3 chords, shorthand figures, basic intervallic logic above the bass.

units.title: Intro to thoroughbass
units.feat: Intervals above bass, key signature, shorthand 5/3

tiers.label: FB-2 — Seventh chords & dissonance
tiers.desc: Progressive introduction of dissonant figures (Handel nos. 1–21): 7, 6/5, 4/2, 9.

tiers.label: FB-3 — Realization as composition
tiers.desc: From figures to improvisation, stylistic realization, and bridge to Roman numerals.

units.title: Figured bass → Roman numerals
units.feat: Retrospective RN labeling; bridge to Tier 2

label: Branch B — Clausulae, Schemata & Partimenti
desc: Historical contrapuntal approach à la Fenaroli. Based on Avner Dorman's Gettysburg counterpoint curriculum. Uses partimento terminology throughout; runs parallel to or before Tier 2.
prereq: Tier 1 complete. Can run concurrently with early Tier 2. P-4 aligns with Tier 2 Units 13–15.

tiers.label: P-1 — Clausulae & simple cadences
tiers.desc: Voice-by-voice construction of cadences. Discant, tenor, bass, alto clausulae.

tiers.label: P-2 — Diminution & sequences
tiers.desc: Diminution techniques, ascending/descending sequences, folia bass.

units.title: Folia bass & variations
units.feat: Vivaldi variation analysis; writing bass variations

tiers.label: P-3 — Compound cadences & schemata
tiers.desc: Double cadences, quiescenza, opening formulae, hexachordal system.

units.title: Hexachordal system
units.feat: Guido, mi-fa, modulation as hexachord shift

tiers.label: P-4 — Rule of the octave & partimenti
tiers.desc: The Fenaroli model: rule of the octave as harmonic grammar, partimento realization.

tiers.label: P-5 — Counterpoint, imitation & fugue
tiers.desc: Three constraint systems, double counterpoint, imitation, fugue from partimento.

units.title: Double counterpoint
units.feat: Invertible counterpoint at octave; over partimento

label: Branch C — Interval Cycles & Slonimsky
desc: Post-tonal optional branch. Interval cycles, combination cycles, and Slonimsky's Thesaurus as compositional and analytical resource.
prereq: Tier 4 Units 29–31 (PC sets, inversional symmetry). Extends into serialism and spectralism.

tiers.label: IC-1 — Interval cycles
tiers.desc: Single-interval cycles: generating collections, symmetry, and cyclic pitch fields.

units.title: Cyclic collections
units.feat: Whole-tone, octatonic, hexatonic as IC cycles

tiers.label: IC-2 — Combination cycles (Slonimsky)
tiers.desc: Slonimsky's Thesaurus: interpolation, ultrapolation, infrapolation; analytical applications.

units.title: Composition with interval & combination cycles
units.feat: Writing etudes using interval and combination cycles

label: Branch D — Neo-Riemannian Theory
desc: Triadic transformations, Tonnetz, and voice-leading geometry. Can follow Tier 3 or run parallel to Tier 4. Strong connection to late Romantic repertoire and triadic post-tonalism.
prereq: Tier 2 complete. Pairs well with Tier 3 chromaticism and Tier 4 PC-set work.

tiers.label: NR-1 — Transformations & Tonnetz
tiers.desc: PLR operations, Tonnetz lattice, hexatonic cycles.

units.title: Compound transformations
units.feat: PL, PR, LR, PLPR chains; Cohn's cycles

units.title: Hexatonic & octatonic poles
units.feat: Hexatonic systems, maximally smooth voice leading

tiers.label: NR-2 — Analysis & extension
tiers.desc: Analytical application and geometric voice-leading spaces.

units.title: NR analysis — 19th-century repertoire
units.feat: Schubert, Brahms, Wagner; chromatic mediant lens

units.title: NR and jazz
units.feat: Parsimonious voice leading in jazz harmony
